rules.rule: GB VED tax class 17 (motorcycles and tricycles, weighing no more than 450kg) lists 'Zero emission motorcycles' as a distinct line from the cc bands, but it is charged the same amount as the smallest cc band (not over 150cc): £27 for a single 12-month payment (rates applying on or after 1 April 2026, per DVLA form V149).

GOV.UK driving licence category A1 is defined by engine size up to 125cc AND power output up to 11kW (no explicit '125cc equivalent' wording found on the page read); A2 by power output up to 35kW; A by power output more than 35kW or power-to-weight ratio more than 0.2kW/kg. Category AM (mopeds) is defined by design speed (over 25km/h but not more than 45km/h), not by a stated kW figure on this page.
rules.quote: Category A1 (Motorcycles): engine size up to 125cc; power output of up to 11kW; power to weight ratio not more than 0.1kW/kg. Category A2: power output up to 35kW, power to weight ratio not more than 0.2kW/kg. Category A: power output more than 35kW or a power to weight ratio more than 0.2kW/kg.

rules.rule: A category B (car) licence holder who passed their car test before 1 February 2001 may ride a moped (up to 50cc) without L-plates, without taking CBT or the full moped test; anything larger than a 50cc moped still requires CBT. A car licence passed on or after 1 February 2001 does not include moped entitlement until CBT (and/or the moped test) is completed.
rules.quote: If you passed your test before 1 February 2001: You can ride a moped (up to 50cc) without L plates. You do not need to take a CBT course or take the full moped test. You must take CBT if you want to ride anything larger than a 50cc moped.

rules.rule: Ireland uses the same EU-derived AM/A1/A2/A structure as GB: AM for mopeds/light quadricycles (min age 16); A1 for motorcycles up to 125cc, power rating not exceeding 11kW, power-to-weight not exceeding 0.1kW/kg (motor tricycles up to 15kW), min age 16; A2 for motorcycles up to 35kW, power-to-weight not exceeding 0.2kW/kg, not derived from a vehicle of more than double its power, min age 18; A for all motorcycles, min age 24 (or 20 with progressive access via A2).
rules.quote: A1: Motorcycles with an engine capacity not exceeding 125 cubic centimetres, with a power rating not exceeding 11 kilowatts and with a power to weight ratio not exceeding 0.1 kilowatt/kg. A2: Motorcycles with a power rating not exceeding 35 kilowatts, with a power to weight ratio not exceeding 0.2 kilowatt/kg and not derived from a vehicle of more than double its power.

rules.rule: ICBC's Basic Insurance Tariff rates motorcycles purely by engine displacement (cc), not by kW or a separate electric category: 110cc or less and Limited speed motorcycle = rate class 310; 111-400cc = 311; 401-750cc = 312; 751-1150cc = 313; over 1150cc = 314. The tariff text found contains no separate provision, kW table, or rate class specifically for electric motorcycles -- the cc-based table is the only motorcycle classification in the document (Schedule B, Table 4.14-A, effective Sept 1 2019, amended to Jan 6 2025).
rules.quote: Table 4.14-A: Motorcycles. Vehicle Use: Limited speed motorcycle (any use) -- Rate Class 310. Motorcycle (any use) Engine displacement 110 cc or less, 111 to 400 cc, 401 to 750 cc, 751 to 1150 cc, Over 1150 cc -- Rate Class 310, 311, 312, 313, 314.

rules.rule: BC defines a 'limited speed motorcycle' (LSM, covers mopeds/scooters) by: a gas motor of not more than 50cc, OR an electric power source producing a maximum of 1.5kW; no clutching/shifting after the drive system engages; max speed on level ground of 70km/h; max weight 95kg excluding fuel/batteries; wheel diameter 254mm or more. An LSM can be ridden on a full-privilege Class 5 or 7 licence (no motorcycle licence required), but must be registered, licensed, insured, and the rider must wear a helmet.
rules.quote: "Limited speed motorcycle" means a motorcycle that: a) is equipped with a motor having a piston displacement of not more than 50 cc or a power source that produces a maximum of 1.5 kW, b) has a power drive system that does not require clutching or shifting by the operator after the drive system is engaged, c) has a maximum attainable speed on level ground, with or without pedals, of 70 km/hour, d) has a maximum weight of 95 kg excluding fuel or batteries used to store energy for vehicle propulsion, and e) has wheels of a diameter of 254 mm or more.

rules.rule: ICBC's own consumer page on mopeds/scooters confirms the same LSM test and states a full-privilege Class 5 or 7 passenger licence (not a motorcycle licence) is sufficient to operate one, with mandatory helmet use.
rules.quote: You can operate an LSM with a full-privilege Class 5 or 7 passenger vehicle licence -- a motorcycle licence is not required. However, the vehicle must be registered, licensed, and insured for road use, and you must always wear a helmet.

rules.rule: Under Mexico City's Código Fiscal de la Ciudad de México, new motorcycles are taxed (Impuesto sobre Tenencia o Uso de Vehículos) at 3% of total value (Art. 161 BIS 9), but electric motorcycles -- new or used -- are explicitly taxed at a 0% rate (Art. 161 BIS 10 for new vehicles in the year of acquisition; Art. 161 BIS 15 for used motorcycles of model year 2002+). Electric cars/motorcycles with an internal-combustion or hydrogen add-on (i.e. hybrids) also get the 0% rate under Art. 161 BIS 10. This tenencia exemption is separate from, and in addition to, a time-limited 2026 subsidy/exoneration program (Jan-Mar 2026) that also forgives the refrendo for motorcycles valued up to $250,000 MXN regardless of powertrain.
rules.quote: ARTICULO 161 BIS 10.- Tratandose de motocicletas electricas, automoviles electricos nuevos, asi como de aquellos electricos nuevos, que ademas cuenten con motor de combustion interna o con motor accionado por hidrogeno, el impuesto se pagara a la tasa de 0%. [...] ARTICULO 161 BIS 15 (used motorcycles, final paragraph): Tratandose de motocicletas electricas, el impuesto se pagara a la tasa de 0%.

rules.rule: The 2026 'control vehicular' notice from the Tesoreria de la Ciudad de Mexico describes the standard 3%-of-value tenencia calculation (with depreciation/updating factors by model year) for motorcycles generally, and instructs that the Derechos por Servicios de Control Vehicular (alta o refrendo -- the registration/renewal fee) must be added on top of whatever tenencia is owed; the document does not state a different alta/refrendo fee for electric motorcycles than for petrol ones -- only the tenencia tax itself differs (to 0%, per Art. 161 BIS 10/15 above).
rules.quote: Al Impuesto sobre Tenencia debera adicionar los Derechos por Servicios de Control Vehicular (alta o refrendo).

rules.rule: California DMV charges a Road Improvement Fee (RIF) on all model year 2020-and-later zero-emission vehicles (ZEVs) at original registration/renewal, currently $121 for 2026; it is not assessed on the very first registration of a newly purchased ZEV from a licensed dealer. The DMV fee page does not itself state whether this applies to motorcycles specifically (it is worded for ZEVs generally); no motorcycle-specific carve-out or exclusion was found on the page read.
rules.quote: The RIF is assessed on all model year 2020 and later zero emission vehicles (ZEV). RIF fees affect vehicle registration renewals unless exempted. [...] RIF is not assessed on the initial registration of a newly purchased ZEV from a licensed vehicle dealer.

rules.rule: New York classifies limited-use motorcycles (mopeds/scooters) into Class A, B, or C purely by top attainable speed, not by engine type: Class A (over 30-40 MPH) needs a Class M motorcycle licence, registration and insurance; Class B (over 20-30 MPH) needs a standard Class D licence, registration and insurance; Class C (20 MPH or less) needs a standard Class D licence and registration but is exempt from compulsory insurance. The same speed thresholds are applied regardless of whether the moped is gas or electric powered.
rules.quote: Class A: over 30-40 MPH. Class B: over 20-30 MPH. Class C: 20 MPH or less.

rules.rule: Connecticut General Statutes section 14-49(b)(1) sets a flat triennial motorcycle registration fee of $63 (of which $6 is earmarked under (b)(2) for Department of Transportation motorcycle rider education) with no separate rate or distinction for electric vs. gasoline motorcycles; the statute's EV-specific fee language elsewhere in 14-49 applies only to passenger motor vehicles, not motorcycles.
rules.quote: For the registration of each motorcycle... the triennial fee shall be sixty-three dollars. [...] Six dollars of the total fee... shall... be deemed to be appropriated to the Department of Transportation [for motorcycle rider education].

rules.rule: Ontario's distinctions for power-assisted/motor-assisted two-wheelers are defined by motor power/speed, not fuel type: a 'power-assisted bicycle' (e-bike) must have a motor of 500W or less with assistance cutting off at 32km/h, needing no licence, registration, plate or insurance. A 'motor-assisted bicycle'/moped must keep working pedals, weigh 55kg or less, and (if internal combustion) not exceed 50cc, with a top speed of 50km/h within 2km from a standing start. A 'limited-speed motorcycle' can exceed 32km/h within 1.6km from a standing start up to a maximum attainable speed of 70km/h. Exceeding the e-bike's 500W/32km/h threshold makes a vehicle a motor vehicle requiring a Class M licence, registration and insurance -- this applies identically to electric and gas-powered machines that cross the thresholds.
rules.quote: A power-assisted bicycle must have an electric motor with a power output rating of 500W or less, and motor assistance must cut off at 32 km/h.

notFound.why: Secondary sources (kennco.ie, odo.ie, autoza.ie) consistently report an 'Electrical motorcycle' annual motor tax rate of EUR 35 alongside 0-75cc EUR49 / 76-200cc EUR67 / 201-9999cc EUR88, but the primary official sources (motortax.ie, citizensinformation.ie) returned HTTP 403 to automated fetch and could not be read directly. The only official gov.ie document retrieved (assets.gov.ie 'Annex E: Motor Tax', an archived 2008/2009 Budget document) shows a different, older schedule with 'Cycles and Tricycles: Electrical EUR31' rather than a dedicated electric-motorcycle line, so it could not be used to confirm the current EUR35 figure. No verbatim quote from an official 2026 source was obtained.

Could not find an official NYS DMV page stating a motorcycle registration fee amount, or any fee differential between electric and gasoline motorcycles; the registration class code page (dmv.ny.gov/registration/registration-class-codes) confirmed electric and gas motorcycles share a single class code (MOT) but did not list fees, and no dedicated fee-schedule page was reached.

No official Ontario.ca or ServiceOntario page was reached stating a registration-fee amount or any difference between electric and gasoline motorcycle registration; only licensing/classification rules (by motor wattage and speed) were confirmed from an MTO-sourced document hosted by Windsor Police.

No official Connecticut Insurance Department or DMV source was found addressing whether electric motorcycles are insurance-rated any differently from gasoline motorcycles; research for this place was limited to the registration-fee statute (CGS 14-49).
